question: Should packaged OpenClaw updates officially preserve local `dist` edits and offer opt-in replay, or should modified installed packages remain unsupported?
rationale: The implementation is defensively engineered, but accepting it establishes a lasting product, compatibility, release-maintenance, and executable-code trust contract that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Preserve and opt-in replay
options.body: Adopt recovery-bundle capture by default and allow explicit trusted replay after integrity and topology checks, then refresh and revalidate the exact merge head.

options.title: Preserve only
options.body: Keep recovery capture and reporting but remove replay, avoiding a supported path that executes restored installed-package edits.

options.title: Reject modified installs
options.body: Keep installed-package mutation unsupported and direct users to reinstall or maintain changes in a source checkout.

recommendation.title: Preserve and opt-in replay
recommendation.body: Adopt recovery-bundle capture by default and allow explicit trusted replay after integrity and topology checks, then refresh and revalidate the exact merge head.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns substantial updater and package-integrity history, is assigned to the PR, and can authorize the permanent support contract.
